newsitem.title: GERMANY: Karstadt gains on fresh takeover rumours.
newsitem.headline: Karstadt gains on fresh takeover rumours.

text.p: Karstadt AG, whose shares have surged about 100 marks this week on a bounty of rumours, kept up its staggering advance on Thursday amid new take-over talk buffeting the beleaguered German retailer.

Karstadt shares touched a new record high at 705 marks at the outset of bourse dealings and were up 27 marks at 690 marks in morning trade, putting them among the best performing shares in the German market.

Some dealers said the extensive gains are particularly puzzling since Karstadt is very likely to be removed from the 30-share DAX index at a German bourse meeting on July 22 and replaced by sportswear group Adidas AG.
Top blue-chip companies that were removed in the past from the DAX index, which takes effect in September, have seen their shares tumble as institutional investors reshuffle portfolios.

One confirmed fact seen supportive for Karstadt is the success of a pilot project at a store in Duisburg where the clothing department was remodelled as part of a new "theme" idea to revamp entire stores. The test has seen double-digit sales growth in the clothing unit on a same-space basis.
Analysts are hoping a broad-based expansion of the project over the next three years will help revive Karstadt, which saw a 2.3 percent drop in first quarter sales to 5.9 billion marks.
But the project is not seen as warranting such hefty gains.
One Frankfurt analyst called the 16 percent rise so far this week from last Friday's closing price at 610 marks "a grotesque overreaction".

"Rumours are popping up every day but this price reaction in Karstadt is well overdone," said Joerg Christians at Trinkaus Capital Markets in Duesseldorf, who rates the Essen-based retailer as a "sell" to take profits.
Dealers said one rumour pushing Karstadt higher on Thursday was that Dutch supermarket group Ahold NV may be interested in buying a stake in Karstadt.
A Karstadt spokesman declined comment on the rumour.

Another rumour that has been helping Karstadt is talk that Germany's WCM Beteiligungs und Grundbesitz AG was still interested in a 25 percent stake despite the group saying in June in a newspaper report that it had no interest.
"The rumour mill around Karstadt will not stop," said Thomas Teetz, analyst at Bankgesellschaft Berlin. "The talk is still that Karstadt is a potential takeover candidate."
Harry Christopoulos, analyst at BZW in Frankfurt, added: "The talk of WCM buying into Karstadt is an old story."

A WCM spokesman was not available for immediate comment. But WCM majority shareholder Karl Ehlerding told the Handelsblatt daily newspaper on June 18 that "we have put acquiring a stake in Karstadt behind us".
WCM had expressed an interest in buying stakes of 10 percent each in Karstadt held by Deutsche Bank AG and Commerzbank AG but pulled out after finding the banks' asking price too high.
Officials at Ahold, which acquired U.S. supermarket chain Stop & Shop last year, were also not immediately available.
But Ahold spokesman Hans Gobes told Reuters in May that Ahold was not interested in Germany and that had not changed.
Ahold also said earlier this month that it intended to seek further expansion on the American east coast and saw healthy growth chances in Asia, Latin America and eastern Europe.

The market is also picking over rumours that Karstadt may be transformed into a holding group and that its units - department store group Karstadt, mail-order group Neckermann and travel group NUR -- would be listed as individual shares.
Analysts put little credence in such a plan.
Calls for Karstadt Chief Executive Walter Deuss, in power since 1979, to resign have also caused its shares to waver.
